reason: Both conversations correctly lead with a 'stop and unplug' safety instruction, but Conversation 1's first turn adds real value: it explains the likely cause (scorched waveguide cover/paint), tells the homeowner to unplug rather than just switch off, and prompts an inspection for burn marks, which surfaced the smoke-from-vents and brown-panel facts. Conversation 2 gives only a generic one-line safety template with no diagnosis, no questions and no direction on replace vs inspect. Conversation 1 is held to only a slight margin because its two follow-up turns degrade into the same irrelevant repeated fire-emergency boilerplate, never answering the sensible 'bin it or check it' question for a £60 unit, though that failure is unhelpful rather than unsafe.
